il_d_pg_wall_coal_house_area.blurb: This wall sits at the Cedar Bluff reserve beside Ferne Clyffe in southern Illinois, reached by taking the right-hand branch of the main trail to the cliff line. It holds 24 roped routes, a near-even split of sport (13) and trad (11) lines. Grades start around 5.7 and run to 5.13, with the bulk in the 5.9 to 5.10 range and a good handful of 5.12s for stronger climbers. The cliff band it belongs to faces south, which makes the neighborhood a decent winter pick on sunny days.

il_b_broken_bridge_area.blurb: Broken Bridge is a small bouldering zone in Lehigh Park near Oglesby, in central Illinois, on a hillside above the river. It has 23 problems, nearly all on the easier side: lots of V1 and a spread through V4, plus one or two hard outliers. Rock quality is mixed, so expect some loose or dirty stone. The walk in from the lot takes roughly half a mile along a river-side trail with some overgrowth and fallen trees, and summer brings thick brush and bugs, so the cooler months are friendlier.

il_a_sex_on_the_beach.blurb: This is the first and best-known boulder cluster on the Mississippi riverbank at The Beach, a couple of miles north of Grand Tower in southern Illinois. The stone is river-smoothed sandstone with sandy landings, and all 23 problems are bouldering, from easy V0s through to a V10, with a strong concentration in the V5 to V7 range. The steepest face is on the south side. There are no trees, so it gets hot with sun for much of the day, and high river water can cover the boulders at times.

il_a_royal_arches_wall.blurb: Royal Arches is the first wall met when walking along the North Falls cliff line at Jackson Falls, in the Shawnee National Forest of southern Illinois. It carries 22 routes, mostly sport (15) with six trad lines and one aid line. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.12, with the weight at 5.10 through 5.12, so it suits intermediate and strong climbers more than novices. Walls in the canyon are around 30 to 70 feet with pockets, slopers and roofs. It holds a lot of routes in a small space and can feel busy on a crowded weekend.

il_a_gill_roof_area.blurb: Gill Roof is the first stretch of cliff reached from the Devils Standtable lot in Giant City State Park, a short graveled walk away in southern Illinois. The sandstone bluff mixes ten boulder problems (V2 to V9, with several in the V4 to V7 range) with sport and trad lines that sit in the beginner to moderate range, roughly 5.3 to 5.8. That makes it handy for families or newer leaders alongside strong boulderers. Many bolted lines start high, so a stick clip is the usual way to reach the first bolt.
